meta.titre: World Biomes and Climate Types: matching plants and ecosystems to the climate that shapes them
meta.sous_theme: Ecosystems, the major biomes and their climates

sections.contenu_markdown: From the green forests of the South Region to the dry grasslands of the far north, a journey across Cameroon crosses very different kinds of vegetation. The same pattern appears on a world scale: each large region of natural vegetation is linked to one type of climate. GCE questions ask you to name the climate of a biome, recognise a climate from its description and locate biomes on a world map. If you learn each biome as a pair of climate and vegetation, these questions become straightforward.

items: Climate is the average weather of a place over many years.
Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius and rainfall in millimetres.
Plants need light, water, warmth and nutrients to grow.
The equator lies at 0° latitude and the tropics are at about 23.5° N and S.

sections.titre: Ecosystems, biomes and the climate types that go with them
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Ecosystem and biome
An **ecosystem** is a community of living things (plants, animals and micro-organisms) together with the non-living environment (soil, water, air, climate) with which they interact. Its main characteristics are the living and non-living parts, a one-way flow of energy from the sun, the recycling of nutrients, food chains in which organisms depend on each other, and a natural balance. A **biome** is a very large ecosystem, named after its dominant vegetation and controlled mainly by climate.

### The main biomes and their climates
| Biome | Climate type | Key climate features | Typical vegetation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tropical rainforest (tropical evergreen) | Equatorial | Hot and wet all year, small temperature range | Tall broad-leaved evergreen trees in layers |
| Savanna (tropical grassland) | Tropical continental (Sudan type) | Hot, with a wet season and a long dry season | Tall grass with scattered trees |
| Hot desert | Hot desert | Very little rain, hot days, cool nights | Xerophytes: cacti, thorny shrubs |
| Mediterranean woodland and scrub | Mediterranean | Hot dry summers, mild wet winters | Evergreen trees with hard, small leaves |
| Temperate deciduous woodland | Cool temperate oceanic | Mild summers, cool winters, rain all year | Oak, beech; leaves fall in autumn |
| Steppe (temperate grassland) | Temperate continental | Hot summers, cold winters, low rainfall | Short grasses, few trees |
| Coniferous forest | Cool temperate continental (Siberian type) | Long, very cold winters, short cool summers | Pine, spruce, fir |
| Tundra | Polar | Very cold, short summer | Mosses, lichens, dwarf shrubs |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how plants are suited to their environment
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give a feature and its use. Xerophytes have waxy leaves, spines and long roots to cut water loss and find water. Rainforest trees are tall and broad-leaved, and use the constant warmth and rain to grow all year. Savanna grasses grow quickly in the wet season, and many trees have thick bark and deep roots to survive dry spells and fire.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you are given monthly temperature and rainfall figures
variantes.contenu_markdown: Total rainfall is the **sum** of the twelve monthly values. Annual temperature range is the **highest monthly temperature minus the lowest**. Count the dry months, then match the pattern: constant heat and rain suggests equatorial; hot with a dry season suggests tropical continental; very little rain suggests desert.

variantes.nom: Locating biomes on a world map
variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must name or mark an area
variantes.contenu_markdown: Tropical rainforest: the Amazon basin, the Congo basin or Indonesia. Savanna: the Sudan belt of Africa, East Africa, northern Australia or the Llanos of Venezuela. Hot desert: the Sahara, the Namib or central Australia. Coniferous forest: northern Canada, Scandinavia and Siberia. Name the area and, if asked, mark it on the correct continent.

sections.enonce_markdown:
The table gives monthly figures for Station X.

| Month | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temperature (°C) | 25 | 27 | 29 | 30 | 28 | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 26 | 25 |
| Rainfall (mm) | 0 | 5 | 20 | 70 | 150 | 210 | 260 | 240 | 180 | 70 | 10 | 0 |

(a) Calculate the total annual rainfall and the annual temperature range. (b) State the climate type and the biome it supports. (c) Describe the rainfall pattern. (4 marks)

etapes.justification: Total rainfall is a sum, not an average.

etapes.action: Find the highest and lowest temperatures.
etapes.justification: Range is the difference between the extremes.
Season patterns identify the climate type.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Rain is concentrated from May to October. 5 months (November to March) have under 25 mm.

etapes.justification: Hot all year with a marked wet and dry season is tropical continental.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: (a) Total rainfall is 1215 mm and the annual temperature range is 5 °C. (b) The climate is tropical continental, which supports savanna grassland of tall grasses and scattered trees. (c) Most of the rain falls from May to October, with a peak in July, and there is a long dry season from November to March when little or no rain falls.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that savanna has an equatorial climate.
items.pourquoi_faux: Equatorial climates are wet all year; savanna has a long dry season.
items.correction_markdown: Link savanna with tropical continental (Sudan) climate and rainforest with equatorial climate.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that xerophytes grow in the rainforest.
items.pourquoi_faux: Xerophytes are plants adapted to dry conditions, so they belong to deserts.
items.correction_markdown: State that xerophytes such as cacti are found in hot deserts, not in wet forests.

items.erreur_markdown: Averaging the rainfall figures when asked for the total.
items.pourquoi_faux: The total is the sum of the monthly values, and an average gives a monthly figure.
items.correction_markdown: Add all twelve values; divide by twelve only when a mean is requested.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that deciduous trees keep their leaves in winter.
items.pourquoi_faux: Deciduous trees shed their leaves in the cold season to save water and energy.
items.correction_markdown: Write that temperate deciduous trees lose their leaves in autumn; coniferous and rainforest trees stay green.

items.erreur_markdown: Marking the tropical rainforest on the world map near 40° N.
items.pourquoi_faux: The rainforest needs heat and heavy rainfall all year, so it lies near the equator.
items.correction_markdown: Place it close to the equator, for example in the Amazon basin or the Congo basin.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the biome that matches each description. (a) Tall grass with scattered flat-topped trees and a long dry season. (b) Cone-bearing evergreen trees in a very cold region. (c) Cacti and thorny shrubs in a very dry area.

Station Y has these figures.

| Month | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temperature (°C) | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 25 | 24 | 24 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 26 |
| Rainfall (mm) | 150 | 160 | 220 | 240 | 250 | 200 | 180 | 190 | 230 | 280 | 220 | 160 |

Calculate (a) the total annual rainfall, (b) the annual temperature range, and (c) name the climate type.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Total rainfall = 150 + 160 + 220 + 240 + 250 + 200 + 180 + 190 + 230 + 280 + 220 + 160 = **2480 mm**.

(b) Range = 27 - 24 = **3 °C**.

(c) Temperatures are high all year with a very small range, and rain is heavy in every month, so the climate is **equatorial**, supporting tropical rainforest.

items.enonce_markdown: Compare the tropical rainforest and the hot desert in terms of climate and vegetation, and explain one way in which plants are adapted in each. (6 marks)
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for points such as:
- Climate: the rainforest is hot and very wet all year, whereas the hot desert has very little rain and a large daily temperature range.
- Vegetation: the rainforest has tall, dense, broad-leaved trees in layers, whereas the desert has sparse, low xerophytes.
- Adaptation in the rainforest: tall trees with large leaves use the constant warmth and rain; buttress roots support them in shallow soil.
- Adaptation in the desert: cacti store water in their stems and have spines and waxy skins to reduce water loss; some plants have long roots to reach deep water.

**Comparisons using words such as whereas earn higher marks than separate descriptions.**

items_markdown: An ecosystem is made of living and non-living parts linked by energy flow, nutrient cycling and food chains; a biome is a very large ecosystem controlled by climate.

Learn each biome with its climate: rainforest with equatorial, savanna with tropical continental, xerophytes with hot desert, deciduous woodland with cool temperate oceanic, steppe with temperate continental, coniferous forest with cool temperate continental (Siberian).
In a climate table, add the rainfall for the total and subtract the lowest temperature from the highest for the range.
Always link a plant feature to the climatic condition it helps the plant survive.
Locate biomes by name of area and continent, using the equator as a reference point.
